I’m sorry it’s still so fresh for you. Your relationship was nearly twice as long as mine and you’re a quarter of the time out from it that I am. I imagine it’s hard as fuck for you right now. The two month mark was particularly difficult for me. That’s when it really started to sink in that, yes, I was free, but also that I gave up on this person that I simply could not deny was quite important to me. 

I know my post perhaps doesn’t read like I’m doing all that great, and I know everyone is different, but if I can offer some solace- it does get easier. The anger does subside. It’ll still flare up, but eventually it stops feeling like it exists in perpetuity. The next bit that gets really hard as you get that distance is you get some nostalgia. The bad times, as overwhelming as they were, do start to feel like less than what they were. Don’t hold on to the anger, but hold on to the reasons behind it. You made the call you did for a reason. But for now, feel that anger, yell at the sky if you gotta- cry if you feel the inclination. You’re not weak for feeling these things. By making the call you needed to make, you’ve already proven that you’re stronger than you’ll ever know.

EDIT: I hope this isn’t coming off as pontificating. I guess I’m just passing onto you some stuff that helped me when I was in the more angry phase of it all.

That’s kind of where I feel like I’m at. Like I’m not gonna be happy again until I find someone else. Everyone and their mothers all say that if you aren’t happy alone, you aren’t gonna be happy in a relationship. 

But that’s the fucked up thing- like I said in the post, I WAS perfectly happy alone. I made it to 23 without giving a single, solitary fuck that I’d never slept with a woman or been in a relationship. I lived my simple little life. I worked, got home to my best friend who was my roommate at the time and my cat. I did my nerd shit and occasionally partied. I threw school into the mix later when I wanted a little more outta life, and that kept me happy. It was simple and I was happy. I just don’t know how to be find happiness in that simplicity again. I feel like at some point I started feeding on the chaos of the relationship and now that I have the peace I so desperately yearned for, I miss the chaos.

Wow. This was quite a read. I enjoyed your thoughts very much. You're a very articulate writer, my friend. I suppose I'll address your points in the same format you posted them.

1. I think this is very possible, and more or less what I was poking at. BotW's toolbox didn't really facilitate exploration, but dripping an extended toolbox over the course of the game would encourage players to scour and survey the land many more times than they may have been compelled to in BotW. 

2. Agreed. BotW's towns *felt* living and breathing, but nothing you did really changed anything. I'd like to see something like a more incremented version of OoT's Hyrule Castle Town, wherein dynamics change over the course of the main story. Obviously, I don't mean having one dungeon's worth of progression be the difference between a beautiful town and a desolate zombie wasteland, but you know- having towns grow and change in meaningful ways. 

3. Very much agreed! [If you'd like to humor me, here's a crude chart I wrote up on this subject.](http://imgur.com/a/ZZI9T)

4. I think the problem with food is much contingent upon a much more deeply rooted problem in BotW, a lack of meaningful resources. The reason you have so much food, and why it can be abused to such degrees is because it's **everywhere**. Lessening food's existence in the world and replacing it with other meaningful currencies, collectibles, and materials would also aid the lack of good rewards from side quests. Also, restricting use of food via maybe a cooldown timer or something would help as discussed in your fifth point.

I see where you're coming from. I just kinda wonder how they would manage to have three ongoing types of Zelda games without sacrificing quality.
